title: Ashmolean Museum: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty paintings and drawings that reveal where an artist concentrated attention.
introduction:
A face may be carefully resolved while the shoulders remain scarcely indicated. A canal can acquire depth from a few ink lines. An isolated arm can show more about the construction of a body than a crowded narrative does. This selection uses the Ashmolean’s paintings and drawings together, so that differing degrees of finish become something to read rather than a simple distinction between complete and incomplete work.

Uccello’s tightly organised hunt provides one starting point; Manet’s broadly handled portrait offers another. Between them are landscapes, literary scenes and likenesses in which the distribution of detail determines what can be known and what remains open.
visitNote: The Ashmolean’s collections extend far beyond the paintings and drawings selected here. Works on paper are sensitive to light and may be in storage or shown only temporarily. Check current displays and loans before planning a visit around a particular object.

books.title: The Practice and Science of Drawing
books.author: Harold Speed
books.note: Speed’s discussions of line and tone provide practical language for the Raphael, Michelangelo, Canaletto and Grünewald drawings. They are most useful when read beside the actual differences in mark and degree of finish.

works.title: The Hunt in the Forest
works.medium: Tempera and oil on panel, with traces of gold
works.credit: Paolo Uccello. The Hunt in the Forest. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The riders and hounds recede among repeated tree trunks toward the forest’s centre. Uccello planned this space with a perspective grid, but the night setting withholds the clear view that such organisation might seem to promise. The museum describes the nocturnal hunt as playful or symbolic rather than a realistic report: precision and invention work together.

works.title: Portrait of a Youth, Possibly a Self-Portrait
works.credit: Raphael. Self Portrait. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The youth’s eyes and cheek receive concentrated shadow while hair and cap can be established with fewer marks. The possible self-portrait identification remains a possibility, not a conclusion supplied by the face’s directness. The drawing is specific as a likeness even while the sitter’s name remains unsettled.

works.title: Andrea Quaratesi
works.credit: Portrait of Andrea Quaratesi. WikiArt; Michelangelo. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The carefully modelled head and more lightly indicated shoulders invite different kinds of attention. Shading gives the face continuity, while the clothing makes fewer claims to a finished surface. Michelangelo lets the drawing develop around its principal encounter; the less resolved areas help disclose where that concentration lies.

works.title: The Exposure of Moses
works.credit: Nicolas Poussin. The Exposure of Moses. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/nicolas-poussin/the-exposition-of-moses
works.description: The child’s position beside the water gives several figures something to respond to, but their gestures do not collapse into one action. Trees and distant buildings extend the setting beyond the group. Poussin uses that room to distinguish responses, making the biblical episode readable through relations among people and places.

works.title: Ophelia
works.credit: Arthur Hughes. Ophelia. Image credit: Arthur Hughes; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Hughes keeps Ophelia upright beside a tree, surrounded by vegetation and holding flowers. The picture should not be confused with the floating figure in Millais’s treatment or Hughes’s earlier seated version. Here the pale standing body is enclosed by growth; the subject’s association with water remains a threat around her rather than a completed event.

works.title: The Daydream
works.credit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti. The Daydream. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/dante-gabriel-rossetti/the-daydream-1878
works.description: The book lies open, but the woman’s attention no longer follows its page. A small branch raised near the hands offers another point of focus. The lightly described setting gives the pause room without explaining it. Interrupted reading is visible; the content of the daydream is not.

works.title: Girl in a Bonnet with Her Head on a Blue Pillow
works.catalogueTitle: Girl in a Bonnet with her Head on a Blue Pillow
works.credit: Anna Alma-Tadema. Girl in a Bonnet with her Head on a Blue Pillow. Image credit: Anna Alma-Tadema; Source credit: https://wsimag.com/art/12787-great-british-drawings. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The cheek rests against the blue pillow, making contact between face and fabric the centre of the image. The bonnet’s ruffles and other pale materials surround that pressure of one soft surface against another. Blue remains emphatic enough for the support to share attention with the person it carries.

works.title: Asolo
works.credit: Edith Corbet. Asolo. Image credit: Edith Corbet; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The buildings do not occupy the view as isolated attractions. Fields and long stretches of ground connect them to a larger inhabited terrain. Corbet’s broad sky permits those intervals to remain important. The town is approached through the land around it, rather than presented as a complete object ready to be inspected.

works.title: Dolo on the Brenta
works.credit: Canaletto. Dolo on the Brenta. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/canaletto/dolo-on-the-brenta
works.description: The waterway connects architecture to use: buildings line it, and modest figures and working structures belong along its edge. The bell tower supplies a clear vertical among the low roofs. Canaletto separates distances sufficiently for small actions to register without making them compete with the whole town.

works.title: The Grand Canal near the Rialto Bridge
works.catalogueTitle: The Grand Canal near the Ponte del Rialto
works.credit: The Grand Canal near the Ponte del Rialto. WikiArt; Canaletto. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Some edges are reinforced by repeated ink strokes while others are left open. Boats, façades and the canal’s direction can be recognised without the continuous surfaces of a finished painting. The drawing makes selection conspicuous: a few decisive lines establish space, and detail accumulates where it is most useful.

works.title: Hester Tradescant and Her Stepson, John
works.catalogueTitle: Hester Tradescant and her Stepson, John
works.credit: Thomas de Critz. Hester Tradescant and her Stepson, John. Image credit: Thomas de Critz; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The meeting of the hands gives the woman and boy a shared point within the foreground. Their different heights and clothing remain distinct around it. The double portrait therefore has more structure than two likenesses placed side by side: a small connection helps hold the family relationship in view.

works.title: Over the Hills of Kurdistan: Flying above Kirkuk
works.catalogueTitle: Over the Hills of Kurdistan: Flying above Kirkuk
works.credit: Sydney Carline. Over the Hills of Kurdistan: Flying above Kirkuk. Image credit: Sydney Carline; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The aircraft wing interrupts the land below, insisting that this elevated view comes from a particular machine. Other aeroplanes share the space above hills and fields. Carline does not offer an unobstructed panorama. Flight changes what can be seen, and the means of seeing it remain within the picture.

works.title: The Poor Actress’s Christmas Dinner
works.credit: Robert Braithwaite Martineau. The poor Actress's Christmas Dinner. Image credit: Robert Braithwaite Martineau; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The small dish claims attention disproportionate to its size because so little else is fully stated. Much of the woman’s body remains lightly indicated around the act of eating. The title proposes poverty as the scene’s condition; the drawing brings that condition close through the scale of the meal rather than a catalogue of missing possessions.

works.title: Katherine and Petruchio
works.credit: Robert Braithwaite Martineau. Katherine and Petruchio. Image credit: Robert Braithwaite Martineau; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The raised vessel and opposing postures turn the furnished room into a place of confrontation. Costume and setting locate the exchange within performed social roles, but gestures make it legible before every literary reference is identified. The scene asks for attention to the physical terms of an argument, not merely the names in its title.

works.title: Thomas Balston
works.credit: Mark Gertler. Thomas Balston. Image credit: Mark Gertler; Source credit: Ashmolean Museum. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The lilac jacket and greenish ground separate sitter from surroundings through colour. Against those broad areas, the head is more precisely described, with the bright tie providing a smaller accent below. The difference in handling gives the face priority without requiring a spotlight or an elaborate account of the sitter’s profession.

works.title: Copse by a Lake in Autumn
works.credit: Isaac Levitan. Copse by a Lake (Autumn). Image credit: Isaac Levitan; Source credit: Art UK. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: The low bank continues through trees, reeds and their darker reflections. Autumn appears in adjustments of colour rather than a dramatic incident or an exceptional landmark. That continuous edge allows small changes to accumulate. The painting offers a season as a condition spread across an ordinary place.

works.title: View on the Nile
works.credit: Thomas Seddon. View on the Nile. Image credit: Thomas Seddon; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The pale sail introduces a diagonal into a view otherwise dominated by the long meeting of bank, water and evening sky. Reflections keep the river connected to distant light. The boats remain particular objects, but they do not close the composition around themselves; the horizontal extent continues beyond them.

works.title: Beech Trees at Sunset, Kensington Gardens
works.catalogueTitle: Beech Trees at Sunset, Kensington Gardens
works.credit: Paul Maitland. Beech Trees at Sunset, Kensington Gardens. Image credit: Paul Maitland; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Tree trunks repeat closely enough to limit the distant view. Depth has to be found in the small lit gaps between them rather than through a broad opening. Maitland gives the garden a contained space, built from repetition and filtered light instead of a single prominent tree or sweeping prospect.

works.title: Portrait of Mademoiselle Claus
works.credit: Édouard Manet. Portrait of Mademoiselle Claus. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/edouard-manet/portrait-of-mademoiselle-claus-1868
works.description: The face is more resolved than the dress and the partly developed figure beside it. A green railing helps hold this unevenly finished arrangement together. Manet’s portrait can therefore be read at two levels: as a likeness and as evidence of decisions still differently visible across the same painted surface.

works.title: Study of an Upper Arm
works.credit: Matthias Grünewald. Upper arm Study. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/matthias-grunewald/forearm-study-1514
works.description: The arm is detached from the larger action it might eventually perform. Chalk and lighter passages are enough to model its curve, making an anatomical fragment available for close study. Isolation changes the task: instead of following a story, attention can remain on how contour and shading give one part of a body force.

closingSections.title: Look where the finish changes
paragraphs: Compare the three early figure drawings with Manet’s portrait and Canaletto’s ink view. Ask what is established first, and what can remain abbreviated without being lost. Works on paper and paintings may have different display arrangements; use the museum’s current records to check availability rather than treating this selection as a fixed itinerary.
